decisions.chain_element: encode neighboring cells as cell sentences

evidence.quote: Specifically, in TISSUENARRATOR each cell is represented as a cell sentence ( Fig. 1A):
o i is the ranked gene sentence, defined as a list of gene symbols ordered by decreasing transcript abundance [16].

decisions.rationale: R6: a cell sentence is a textual representation serialized from gene data.

decisions.chain_element: assemble them into a spatial sentence

evidence.quote: cells with their cell sentences { s i } n i =1 were assembled in pre-determined spatial order to construct one spatial sentence

decisions.rationale: R6: separately produced cell sentences are assembled into one ordered spatial sentence.

decisions.chain_element: serialize the perturbed cell and its context

evidence.quote: The natural-language spatial sentences are then used to fine-tune an LLM to learn cell and text generation through next-token prediction.
During inference, TISSUENARRATOR was given a single unseen perturbed cancer cell and tasked with generating the gene expression of its neighboring T cells.

decisions.rationale: R6: the perturbed cell and contextual information are represented in a spatial-sentence text format.

decisions.chain_element: predict the target cell given the perturbed neighbor

evidence.quote: Predicting effects of genetic perturbation: TISSUENARRATOR predicts a target cell given an edited or perturbed neighboring cell, expanding known single-cell perturbation effects to tissuelevel responses.

decisions.rationale: R1: this element states the model task performed for genetic perturbation.

decisions.chain_element: serialize the neighborhood as a spatial sentence

evidence.quote: For each spatial neighborhood j , cells with their cell sentences { s i } n i =1 were assembled in pre-determined spatial order to construct one spatial sentence
This design is partially inspired by GeST [38], with two key improvements.

decisions.rationale: R6: the neighborhood is formatted as a natural-language spatial sentence.

decisions.chain_element: predict the target cell within the altered neighborhood

evidence.quote: Predicting response to neighborhood composition: TISSUENARRATOR predicts a target cell within a neighborhood with counterfactual cell-type composition, enabling in silico perturbations such as adding or removing neighbor cells.

decisions.rationale: R1: this element states the model task performed under counterfactual neighborhood composition.

parameters.name: order
parameters.value: genes ranked by gene expression level

decisions.chain_element: transform each cell into cell sentences

evidence.quote: TISSUENARRATOR starts by transforming each cell into the natural language space by encoding gene expression as 'cell sentences', a list of genes ranked by gene expression level.

decisions.rationale: R6: each cell is transformed into a textual cell-sentence representation.

evidence.quote: All cell sentences in a tissue patch are then assembled into a 1D 'spatial sentence', where cells are serialized by proximitybased traversal.

decisions.rationale: R6: cell-sentence sequences are joined in the stated proximity-based traversal order.

evidence.quote: given the name of an anatomical structure, (1) return the top 5 most abundant cell types, (2) list the top 20 highly expressed genes, and (3) generate a natural-language description of the structure.
TISSUENARRATOR generalizes to unseen anatomical structure names in natural language queries by building on the pretrained knowledge of its LLM backbone.

decisions.rationale: R6: the anatomical-structure input is rendered as a natural-language question.

decisions.chain_element: fine-tune on questions derived from held-out structures

evidence.quote: We split the dataset by structure name, fine-tuned TISSUENARRATOR, and evaluated the model on questions derived from held-out structures.

decisions.rationale: R1: this element describes task-specific training and held-out evaluation data.
